# a11y.lang-parts — lang on an inner element is not a valid language code

- **Check ID:** `a11y.lang-parts`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 3.1.2
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/a11y.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/a11y.lang-parts.md`](../a11y.lang-parts.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A `lang` attribute on an element inside the page is not a valid language code.

## Why it matters

When a passage is in a different language from the rest of the page, `lang` tells screen readers to switch pronunciation. A French quotation read in an English voice is nearly unintelligible. That only works when the code is valid: `lang="english"`, `lang="en_US"`, and `lang="fr-"` are ignored, so the passage is read in the page language.

## What it checks

Every `lang` attribute on an element other than `<html>` (the page language is checked by [`meta.lang`](meta.lang.md)). A value is valid when it is a BCP 47 language code: a 2 or 3 letter language, optionally followed by hyphen-separated subtags of up to 8 letters or digits (`fr`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hant-TW`), or a private-use tag starting `x-`. An empty `lang=""` is allowed, because HTML uses it to say the language is unknown. The check does not look up whether the code is registered.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before -->
<blockquote lang="french">Je pense, donc je suis.</blockquote>
<p lang="en_US">Colour</p>

<!-- after -->
<blockquote lang="fr">Je pense, donc je suis.</blockquote>
<p lang="en-US">Color</p>
```

The report gives an exact edit when the only problem is an underscore. For other values, use the short code for the language (`fr`, `de`, `ar`, `fa`, `es`), or remove the attribute if the text is in the page language.

## Options

None.
